institution: Indian Council of Medical Research, Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance and Research Network (AMRSN)
page: https://www.icmr.gov.in/reports (Antimicrobial Resistance section); flipbooks for 2017-2021 at https://iamrsn.icmr.org.in/index.php/resources/amr-icmr-data
citation: ICMR. Annual Report: Antimicrobial Resistance Research and Surveillance Network, January 2023 to December 2023. New Delhi: Division of Descriptive Research, Indian Council of Medical Research; 2024.
reporting: Percent susceptible with n/N tested. Specimen-wise antibiograms by location (OPD, ward, ICU) for blood, urine and pus/exudates (chapter 2); Enterobacterales from all specimens except urine and faeces, by species and by location, and from urine by species; carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets; non-fermenters from all samples by location and by specimen (blood, LRT, SI, DI, CSF, urine). Colistin given as percent intermediate in chapters 3 and 4; cells with few isolates tested are printed as '(-)'.
method: CLSI guidelines using disc diffusion or automated systems, colistin by broth microdilution (PDF page 76); breakpoint edition not stated. Data from tertiary-care network hospitals; the report says it does not reflect community AMR (PDF page 5).

verification.note: Part 1: Part A of the report (chapter 1 organism counts, chapter 2 specimen-wise antibiograms of Enterobacterales and non-fermenters, chapters 3 and 4). Every susceptibility table was parsed from the PDF text layer with pdfplumber (no retyping), every cell was checked arithmetically (printed n/N against the printed %), and every value was then compared by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 2.6 (wide tables cut into two or three crops): Tables 2.7 to 2.9, 2.11 to 2.13, 2.16, 2.18 to 2.20, 3.1 to 3.5, 3.14, 3.19, 3.20, 4.1, 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 4.7, 4.8, 4.10 and 4.11. Count Tables 1.3, 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 were parsed from the text layer and compared by eye; Tables 2.2 to 2.4 were read from the page images and checked against the chapter 1 specimen totals. Source inconsistencies are recorded as printed with conflict entries or notes (colistin in Tables 2.11 to 2.13 and 2.16, the repeated colistin cell of Table 3.1, S. maltophilia OPD levofloxacin, denominators above the column n in Tables 3.19 and 3.20, sample-wise n in Tables 4.2 and 4.5). Part 2: Part B (chapter 2 tables for Part B organisms, chapters 5 to 10). Every table was parsed from the PDF text layer by script (pdfplumber tables, word boxes for Table 7.2, no retyping) and then compared value by value by eye against page renders at scale 2.2 to 3.0, cropped by table or half-table: Tables 2.10, 2.14, 2.15, 2.17, 2.21, 2.22, 5.1, 6.1, 6.3, 6.8, 7.1, 7.2, 7.5 to 7.7, 7.10, 7.12 to 7.14, 8.1 to 8.4, 9.2 to 9.4, 10.27 to 10.29, 10.39 and 10.40. Every printed n/N was checked arithmetically against its printed percentage; the OPD, ward and ICU counts of Tables 7.2 and 7.14 add up exactly to their Total columns, and Tables 2.14 and 2.15 add up to Table 7.13. The 2023 columns of the trend tables were compared with the tables used. Contradictions of 1 percentage point or more are recorded as conflict entries; smaller ones as notes.

notes: ICMR AMRSN 2023, part A: organism counts (chapter 1 and chapter 2 section A), specimen-wise antibiograms by location for E. coli, K. pneumoniae, A. baumannii and P. aeruginosa (chapter 2 section B), Enterobacterales (chapter 3) and non-fermenting Gram-negative bacilli (chapter 4). 99,492 culture-positive isolates from the network's tertiary-care centres. Enterobacterales rows are 'all specimens except urine and faeces' (spec nonurine) by location, urine rows are all locations; non-fermenter rows are 'all samples (except faeces)' (spec all) by location and by specimen. Chapter 2 rows give blood, urine and pus/exudates by location (no all-location column); pus/exudates is one specimen type within the report's superficial infections, so these pus rows and counts are narrower than the chapter 4 pus (superficial infection) rows. Colistin figures are percent intermediate (chapters 3 and 4 footnotes; chapter 2 prints no footnote), and in chapter 2 several printed colistin percentages disagree with their own counts (recorded as printed, with conflicts). CR and CS rows are carbapenem-resistant and carbapenem-susceptible subsets. The sample-wise non-fermenter tables (4.2, 4.5) print an n per specimen that matches the numbers tested, well below the isolate counts of Table 1.10. Counts: Table 1.3 by location (all specimens), Tables 1.5, 1.10, 1.13 and 1.17 by specimen (all locations), and the top-5 lists of Tables 2.2 to 2.4 by specimen and location (blood, urine, pus/exudates); the sets overlap, so their sum is not an isolate total. CoNS counts are the Table 1.13 CoNS total; Enterococcus spp. counts are the unspeciated group of Table 1.17. ICMR AMRSN 2023, part B: typhoidal Salmonella (blood), diarrhoeal pathogens (stool), staphylococci and enterococci, fungi, S. pneumoniae (national reference laboratory isolates) and ICU HAI surveillance susceptibility (cohort "hai"), plus the chapter 2 location tables for these organisms (S. Typhi blood, enterococci urine, S. aureus pus/exudates, faecal Salmonella and Aeromonas). 99,492 culture-positive isolates in the network in 2023. Cells printed as "(-)" (too few isolates) or as counts without a percentage are left out. Several percentages are printed about 0.05 above the count ratio (e.g. 50/415 printed 12.1); recorded as printed. The yearly trend tables (2017 to 2023) are not recorded: the 2024 edition covers 2017 to 2024.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample (sample_cells.py, 239 cells) plus a seeded top-up that takes the chapter 2 specimen-by-location Tables 2.7 to 2.9, 2.11 to 2.13, 2.16 and 2.18 to 2.20 to 40% of their cells (295 sampled cells in all) was read from page images (scale 2.6 to 4.5, cropped by column group) before the extracted values were looked at; every table was in fact read in full, so all 955 cells (printed percentage and number tested), all 100 row n with organism, specimen, location and phenotype, and all 198 counts were compared with the file. 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected, so no table needed a re-read under the 2% rule. The cells the validator lists (values seen in its output first) were re-read in zoomed crops.

Location columns: every chapter 2 table prints OPD, ward, ICU in that order, and its column n match the location counts of Tables 2.2 to 2.4 wherever those list the organism (all but A. baumannii blood OPD), except P. aeruginosa pus ICU (below). Table 4.7 prints Total, Ward, ICU, OPD and is mapped correctly (OPD n=163). No OPD/ward/ICU swap found anywhere.

Conflicts confirmed as printed: colistin in Table 2.11 (1945/1970 printed 99.7%, 967/978 printed 99.6%, 305/305 printed 99.6%), Table 2.12 (535/554 97.3%, 450/484 96.1%, 170/173 94.4%), Table 2.13 (195/198 95.4%, 237/246 95.8%, 97/102 97.3%) and Table 2.16 ICU (117/177 printed 100); Table 3.1 colistin 305/327 (93.3) printed identically in the E. cloacae, Enterobacter spp. and P. mirabilis columns (the chapter text on PDF page 76 gives 93.3% for E. cloacae, so keeping the cell on E. cloacae and flagging the other two columns is right); S. maltophilia OPD levofloxacin 76/85 printed (88.4). Every conflict text quotes the right counts.

Other cells the validator does not keep are printed as recorded: fosfomycin in blood (E. coli 30/31, 71/73, 30/30; K. pneumoniae 9/14, 44/63, 39/75); intrinsic E. cloacae urine cefazolin 3/30 (10.0), P. mirabilis urine nitrofurantoin 5/68 (7.4), M. morganii urine nitrofurantoin 4/32 (12.5) and P. mirabilis colistin (the repeated cell above); hidden E. coli CR and CS nitrofurantoin 22/39 (56.4) and 67/77 (87.0).

The 15 count-table mismatches are printed that way (source, not transcription): P. aeruginosa pus ICU 122 in Table 2.4 against n=121 in Table 2.20; E. coli urine 10043 in Tables 1.2 and 1.5 (and 6022 + 3411 + 610 in Table 2.3) against n=10042 in Table 3.14; A. baumannii 11947 in Tables 1.2 and 1.3 (1260 + 6086 + 4601) against 11948 in Tables 1.10 and 4.1; and the 12 specimen columns of Tables 4.2 and 4.5, whose printed n is the number tested (A. baumannii blood 1270, LRT 3519, SI 1080, DI 334, CSF 156, urine 228; P. aeruginosa 583, 2262, 1663, 399, 40, 707), against the Table 1.10 isolate counts. Each already has a row note. (build-antibiogram.mjs was updated while this check ran and now lists 14: it no longer flags the A. baumannii pair, whose 11947 is a sum of location counts.)

Also confirmed against the pages: the cells printed as (-) and left out, the Klebsiella spp. columns of Tables 3.1 and 3.14, the Total columns of Tables 3.2 to 3.5 and the all-specimen columns of Tables 4.8 and 4.11 (identical to Table 3.1 and to the Total columns of Tables 4.7 and 4.10), the denominator notes of Tables 3.19 and 3.20, Table 1.2 LRT 5575 against 5576 in Table 1.10, and the polymyxin B and ticarcillin-clavulanate cells listed in excluded. Two rounding-only differences are rightly left without a conflict (Table 2.18 ward colistin 284/287 printed 98.9; Table 4.4 total colistin 2923/3037 printed 96.3). Counts not recorded (S. haemolyticus, S. epidermidis, S. hominis, S. Typhi, Klebsiella spp.) are listed in excluded with reasons. verification.status left as double-checked.

Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell of every extracted table re-read by eye from page renders (scale 2.5 to 4, dense tables cropped by column group) and written down before comparing with the file: all 840 cells with their printed number tested (the seeded 25% sample of 210 cells from sample_cells.py is part of this), all 104 row n, and every cell printed as (-), -, NT or counts only (all correctly left out). As asked, the chapter 2 location tables (2.10, 2.14, 2.15, 2.17, 2.21, 2.22) and the HAI tables (10.27 to 10.29, 10.39, 10.40) were read in full; Table 10.41 is counts only (N=6, 'numbers too low') and rightly excluded.

Second reader: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected: no wrong value, n or number tested, no OPD/ward/ICU column swap, no organism, phenotype or cohort mix-up (every HAI row has cohort hai; the chapter 2 urine ICU enterococcal rows of Tables 2.14 and 2.15 stay separate from the HAI UTI rows of Table 10.40), and every row's table and page are right. No table needed a correction re-read.

Second reader: the 2 cautions are printed that way: Table 7.1 S. aureus oxacillin 1689/4072 (35.9), confirmed at zoom, while Tables 7.2 (Total) and 7.4 (2023) print 1737/4071 (42.7); Table 10.39 E. coli UTI colistin 86/95 (93.5). The 7 intrinsic cells are printed as recorded: C. krusei fluconazole 15/40 (37.5) in Table 8.1 and 6/19 (31.6) in Table 8.2; HAI BSI K. pneumoniae ampicillin 3/136 (1.5), A. baumannii amoxicillin-clavulanate 3/26 (11.5), ampicillin 2/32 (6.3) and ertapenem 2/26 (7.7); HAI UTI K. pneumoniae ampicillin 1/26 (3.9). The 1 hidden cell, HAI UTI E. coli tigecycline 23/25 (92.0) (hidden by the urine tigecycline rule), is printed as recorded. The file has no count tables, so there are no count mismatches.

Second reader: every printed percentage re-computed from its printed counts. Only 6 are 0.5 points or more off, all printed that way and all already recorded: the 2 conflicts above, and as notes HAI BSI K. pneumoniae ampicillin 1.5 (3/136 = 2.2), HAI BSI E. coli tetracycline 30.1 (13/42 = 31.0), Table 7.6 MRSA clindamycin 66.2 (1225/1833 = 66.8) and Table 9.4 levofloxacin 96 (87/90 = 96.7).

Second reader: S. pneumoniae split checked against Tables 9.2 and 9.3 (p210 to 211): the CSF row (n=11) is the meningeal-criteria column, penicillin 3/11 (27.27) and cefotaxime 9/11 (81.80); the blood row's penicillin 62/63 (98.41) and cefotaxime 63/63 (100) are the 63 non-meningeal isolates, and its other six agents and its n=74 are Table 9.3 (all invasive isolates). Values and numbers tested match the page. Two judgement calls, both stated in the row notes and left as they are: the page does not say the 11 meningeal isolates are CSF isolates (meningeal is the breakpoint set), and the 74 invasive isolates include those 11 and come from blood, CSF and sterile fluids (p207), so the blood row stands for all invasive isolates.

Second reader: stratum calls and note cross-references checked on the pages and correct: Table 6.3 is headed 'All Specimens' but its S. flexneri counts are exactly the OPD plus ward faecal counts of Table 2.23, so stool is right; 'Salmonella spp. Faecal' (Table 1.27: 307 isolates, OPD 96, ward 210, ICU 1) is the group Table 1.28 calls 'Non Typhoidal Salmonella' (307/773 in 2023); Table 5.4 prints S. Paratyphi A levofloxacin 4/19 as 21.1; Table 6.6 has only the V. cholerae column, all (-); Table 10.45 does repeat identical counts across many agents, as its exclusion says.

CoNS species rows added 2026-09-26 (antibiogram-rules.js now has species keys): Table 7.10 (p176, 'CoNS isolated from all specimens', no location split; spec all, set all, like its S. saprophyticus row) columns S. haemolyticus (n=2262), S. epidermidis (n=2056) and S. hominis (n=1408), 9 cells each (27 in all) with n/N as printed. First reading from the text layer (pdfplumber words assigned to cells by the table's grid lines), second from the page image (scale 3.4, first three species columns cropped in two halves); the two agreed on all 27 percentages, 27 n/N and 3 n, and every n/N gives its printed percentage. The excluded entry for these columns was removed.
